title: WPL mini-auction: Sneh Rana among the biggest names as 146 players go under the hammer
summary: Australia's T20 World Cup-winning captain Sophie Molineux is also in the pool.
image_credit: File photo: India women's team. Photo: India / [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:India_women%27s_national_cricket_team_poses_with_the_2025_Women%27s_Cricket_World_Cup_trophy_at_7,_Lok_Kalyan_Marg.jpg), GODL-India
body:
146 players are in the Women's Premier League mini-auction on October 28. Off-spinning all-rounder Sneh Rana, released by Delhi Capitals, is one of the biggest names.

Other headline names include Australia's T20 World Cup-winning captain Sophie Molineux, along with Grace Harris and Jess Jonassen.

India middle-order batter Tejal Hasabnis, who did well for India A against Australia A last month, is also expected to draw interest.

The auction is being held at the Grand Hyatt in Kochi. Only 27 places are available across the five teams, and 20 of them are reserved for Indian players.

UP Warriorz go in with the biggest purse, Rs 3.75 crore. Gujarat Giants have Rs 1.25 crore, Royal Challengers Bengaluru Rs 1.15 crore, Delhi Capitals Rs 1.1 crore and Mumbai Indians Rs 90 lakh.

Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu and England opener Sophia Dunkley are also in the pool. Capped Indian players on the list include G Kamalini, Kiran Navgire, Uma Chetry, Taniya Bhatia, Saika Ishaque, Asha Sobhana, Priya Mishra, Titas Sadhu and Saima Thakor. Among the uncapped players is 16-year-old Ira Jadhav, who scored an unbeaten 346 off 157 balls for Mumbai against Meghalaya in last year's Women's Under-19 One-Day tournament.

Hasabnis got only one chance in India's ODI series against Zimbabwe and lasted five balls. The third match of that series is being played in Vadodara on the same day as the auction.

The Women's Premier League is the BCCI's professional women's T20 league. It started in 2023 with five city-based teams, and since 2026 it has been played in January and February. Mumbai Indians and Royal Challengers Bengaluru have each won the title twice in the four seasons so far.
